review: Request: at round 12 Wren (outdoors on ordinary soil, energy 39.3, holding 2.9 roots) asked for a small controllable heat source for nearby physical heating trials, with a safe way to put it out and its fuel, duration, reach, burn and spread risks stated and no automatic cooking, safety or reward, after a root heat probe failed because no heat source was within reach. World Agent decision: develop (learning 4) a general operate-small-combustion-source operation with attempt-ignition, tend, inspect and extinguish modes: direct friction only where supplied pieces have suitable geometry and grip, no stone sparks and no invented cordage or tools, a second ignition mode from an existing hot target, represented fuel mass, moisture and heat yield, a persistent process that leaving or death does not stop, study 4 rounds, an ignition attempt of 1-5 rounds at 1 energy per active round within a declared mechanical-work budget, tend and hot-target ignition 1 round and 0.5 energy, inspect 1 round and 0.2 energy through probe, extinguish 1 round and 0.5 energy plus real material, an executable way to put it out and an inspection of the surroundings before ignition, and, as blocking dependencies to implement now, a mass and heat ledger, ignition and burn rules, oxygen and heat losses, heat transfer to nearby objects and actors, and quench, smother and burn-risk handling. Reuse check: local-fire@1 (forest-fire.ts) cannot be installed in this world: it has no scope, so the development registry omits it and v7Install rejects it as not approved for the experiment scope; it depends on the equally unscoped active-warming@1; its migration wires the thermal-refuge satisfaction source; it has no friction geometry, material smothering, spread or burn rule; and no earlier long or development run installed it (the ex17 and ex18 heat packages are scoped to their own runs). Implemented: a new package small-combustion-source@1 (scope long-ex21, ability operate-small-combustion-source, handler long.small-combustion-source, learning 4, no study energy) that reuses local-fire and ex17 values through long-thermal-physics.ts (BURN, DRILL, HEAT and drillRound, unchanged), the ex19 material checks, the collective-work escrow and paid-work helpers, openRemember and the baseline probe observe; every existing package stays byte-identical. tend (1 round, 0.5 energy) lays a new non-solid 0.2 m bed at x,y in reach on firm ground (not water, a wet bank, waterlogged or saturated soil) under open sky with no solid object, other bed or person on the footprint, or feeds the builder's own bed; it takes quantity (default 1) from each named own fuel item (inedible with a represented fuel value; food is refused) and tinder item (combustible, at most 0.3 kg a unit, flexibility 5 or more: dry grass, bark, moss, reed), up to 1.6 kg in the bed. inspect (anyone in reach) calls probe observe for its own 0.2 energy and keeps an unverified personal record of the state, a bed temperature reading with a declared uncertainty of the larger of 5 K and 10%, fuel and water shares, readiness, weather, exposed combustibles within 0.45 m, people within 2 m and the cover needed. attempt-ignition needs the builder's unlit, uncovered bed with at least 0.5 tinder and 0.5 other fuel (the local-fire minimums), the igniter's own inspection of it within 10 rounds, and owned sand or clay totaling 2.01 kg named in extinguishingItemIds (checked, not reserved). friction: toolItemIds names a rubbing piece and a base, each a whole own rigid wood unit (fuel value 7 or more, hardness 3 or more, flexibility at most 3, unfractured, the rubbing piece not softer); the declared v1 geometry treats a whole unit as a round rod of green wood at 900 kg/m3 and 25 diameters long (a branch is 4.0 cm by 1.0 m), the rubbing piece needs a 1.5-5 cm two-hand grip, the base 3 cm for a groove, both 0.3 m of length; stone and other materials are refused, since stone strikes give no sparks here; both pieces are reserved for durationRounds 1-5 (default 3) and each worked round is paid at 1 energy through workPay; under the declared conversion of 21.6 kJ of hand work per energy (the ex17 20 W over the 1080 s round) the ex17 contact law applies unchanged: peak = air + 15 K per earlier consecutive round + contact x dryness x 20 W / (0.04 W/K x (1 + 0.5 x wind)), dryness 1 - water/0.35, contact 0.5 rising to 1 as a 1.5 mm a round groove wears; each round wears 0.5 g from the rubbing piece and 1.5 g from the base, whose solids become dust and whose water leaves as vapour, with a per-round work ledger (work, vapour, dust heat, loss); an ember needs 350 C with 2 g of dry dust and lights the tinder only at a tinder water share of at most 0.35, rain at most 0.15 and wind at most 0.65, a first flame burning 0.1 tinder, otherwise the ember dies; the attempt ends with worn pieces and no refund after the requested rounds, on an unworked round, lost reach or energy, or death (pieces dropped where the person died); the base keeps its groove. hot-target (1 round, 0.5 energy) lights the bed from its own retained heat at 300 C or more, or from a 0.1-unit brand carried from the person's own burning bed whose centre lies within 1 m. extinguish (anyone in reach, 1 round, 0.5 energy) covers a burning or hot bed with the tenths of the person's listed sand or clay needed for 2.01 kg (a 1 cm layer over the bed at 1600 kg/m3), or quantity from each; the material is consumed into the bed, combustion stops, the cover shares the bed heat, its water boils off above 100 C, and the event reports absent combustion and the residual bed reading; a later inspection reading within 5 C of the air verifies cold residue. Only the builder may feed or light a bed; anyone may inspect or smother it; nobody else is controlled. Process, every round whoever is present: rain wets bed fuel by 0.08 x rain and above 0.6 douses the fire; exposed loose combustible items and one unit a round of combustible standing stock within 0.45 m of a burning bed catch and join it (the ex17 rim rule at the bed radius plus 0.25 m); at most 1 fuel unit (2 MJ) a round burns times (1 - water), tinder first, 10% of burned solids as ash and 90% as exhaust, their water as vapour; burning fuel dries by 0.08 water share a round paid from the heat; embers last 3 rounds after the last burn; released heat goes to vapour, a fifth into the bed (800 J/K, 0.6 W/K loss), a tenth to the near field and the rest to the surroundings; people within 2 m on a clear line receive the local-fire warmth 0.6 x burn fraction x (1 - d/2) x (1 - 0.5 x wind) degrees before thermal damage, limited by the near-field share at 245 kJ a degree, so overheating harms under the existing rule; a body on a burning bed loses 5 x burn fraction health, recorded as injury; probe heat trials in reach draw 0.1 MJ each from the stored bed heat, offered as availableHeat. Events: small-fire-bed-laid, -fed, -inspected, -cooled, -friction-worked, -friction-ended, -ember-formed, -ember-died, -ignition-failed, -ignited, -burned, -spread, -doused, -flame-out, -smothered, -heat-received and -actor-burned, with view metadata (source, position, footprint, hazard radius, state, active mode, progress, flame only while burning, flame intensity, smoke, embers, cover, fuel mass, bed temperature, residue); no new drawing is declared (visualComponents empty) and observers see only the public mode and progress (createdBy null). Modeling assumptions: fuel and piece water is the represented water share (branch 0.5, dry grass 0.4) or an explicit composition, and no rule here dries material except fuel in a burning bed; heat yield per unit is the resource fuel value times 2 MJ regardless of water; the 21.6 kJ energy conversion, rod geometry and grip limits, 1.6 kg capacity, bed values and shares, 245 kJ a degree, 5 health a round, 0.45 m exposure, a 2.01 kg cover of sand or clay only, 300 C retained-heat ignition, 10-round inspection validity, the 5 C cold margin and the reading uncertainty are declared values; oxygen is the local-fire open-air rate and a cover closes it; water quenching is not offered because no water container exists here; unburned friction dust stays as residue; tending does not separate pieces or partly cover the bed; no pleasure or reward is added, records are unverified and the ignition event never qualifies a practice milestone; nothing is cooked or otherwise changed in food. Throwaway check on the archived round-12 world: Wren can learn it in 4 rounds, the roots are refused as fuel, Wren can gather branches, dry grass and wet clay (about 45 rounds of travel, gathering and rest), lay and inspect a bed, but a 5-round friction attempt with the gathered branches reaches only about 85 C because their represented water share is 0.5, so it fails with 5 energy spent and worn pieces, and the represented dry grass (0.4) could not take an ember either; the tests show ignition, burning, heat, probing, smothering, spread and burns with air-dried test compositions. Also changed: forest-environment.ts gains two calls gated by this revision (warmth before thermal damage, burns after it), and the ex21 air-dry test's registry assertion now admits later ex21 packages. First release: no; the specification is self-consistent and implementable, so this is a real mechanism with real costs, state changes and events, whose honest present outcome for Wren is a failed friction attempt on wet wood.
